verdict.rationale: Kintsugi's docs say every product is classified into a category and subcategory, and that this classification drives taxation across jurisdictions. Tax estimates also account for product taxability. The evidence does not show the developer-facing mapping mechanism or the specific category taxonomy, so this is partial. Missing for 10: documented API or SDK fields for assigning catalog items to categories, an explicit taxonomy covering SaaS/digital goods/services/physical products, per-line-item taxability in transaction payloads, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can map my catalog to the vendor's tax categories — SaaS, digital goods, services, physical products — so each line item is taxed by what it is, in every jurisdiction it sells

citations.quote: Kintsugi classifies every product into a **category** and **subcategory**, which together determine how it is taxed across jurisdictions.
Rates reflect your nexus, your product taxability, your customer's exemptions, and the address you are shipping to.
